finding.problem: Report promises monotonic cooperative stop handling through terminal stdout/exit. Actual outer finally restores TERM/INT handlers before final stopping check, actual_exit calculation, print and sys.exit. A late TERM or KeyboardInterrupt can yield nonzero external exit with a prior disk PASS remaining. This is a report/acceptance boundary mismatch; it is not evidence of a live child leak or product defect.
finding.minimalRepair: Make the terminal contract exact and ensure acceptance requires the captured outer process exit0 plus complete matching final stdout plus sealed result/budget and both child exits. Choose one narrow solution: keep stop handling through the declared terminal output/decision boundary and reconcile a handled late stop to FAILED/nonzero; or document an explicit earlier completion linearization boundary, remove the unsupported through-exit claim, and state that any missing/failed external exit receipt invalidates an on-disk PASS. Do not claim immunity to SIGKILL/power loss or add a general supervisor framework.
finding.important: Simply moving handler restore later while reusing an already-computed exit0 is insufficient for a promised late-stop guarantee.
